title: Leaf Boat Regatta
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: float leaf boats in a bowl of water and see which leaf makes the best boat.

body.heading: Choose your boats
paragraphs: Collect fallen leaves of different shapes and sizes — a wide leaf, a long leaf, and a curled leaf make a good racing fleet.
Leaves float because they are light and spread their weight over the water. A curled leaf works like a tiny boat hull.

body.heading: Launch the fleet
paragraphs: Fill a big bowl or tub with water and float your leaves. Watch which leaf sits highest and which one wobbles.
Load each boat with tiny bits of grass, one piece at a time. How much cargo can each boat carry before it sinks? Count the pieces.

body.heading: Crown the winner
paragraphs: The best boat is not always the biggest. A wide, curled leaf often beats a huge flat one that lets water wash over its edges.
When the regatta ends, tip the water on the garden. Your boats can sail again another day, or rest in the compost.

takeaway: Wide, curled leaves make the best boats because they spread out and keep the water out.
materials: A big bowl or tub of water
Tiny bits of grass for cargo
safetyNotes: Only use fallen leaves, and wash your hands after playing. An adult should carry and place the water bowl.
screenFreeExtension: Blow gently through a straw to make wind and sail your leaf boat across the bowl.
